about: Etch rates used by every scene. Edit this file, then run npm run build: the build checks it (tools/validate-data.mjs) and puts it into index.html. Rates are stored in the unit of the source; the page converts them to µm/min. See docs/DATA.md.

PalSato4.1.note: 12 orientations at 30, 40 and 50 wt%. Columns are keyed by concentration in wt%.

Q.source: Q(100) 0.60 eV: Pal & Sato p. 90 (40 % KOH); Seidel et al. 1990 give 0.57, 0.59 and 0.61 eV for 20, 42 and 57 % KOH (Fig. 12, p. 3618). Q(110) 0.59 eV: Seidel et al. 1990, Fig. 17, p. 3620 (20 % KOH; 0.57 eV for (100) in the same run). Q(111): no number in the sources, 0.60 eV (assumption); the sources disagree on its direction: Pal & Sato p. 90 say {111} has the smallest Q, Seidel et al. 1990 (abstract, p. 3612) find higher Q for slowly etching planes. Q(SiO₂) 0.85 eV: Seidel et al. 1990, Fig. 18, p. 3620 (0.85 eV in 20 % and 0.86 eV in 42 % KOH).

etchants.name: EDP Type S, 110 °C (Lec 10)
etchants.source: Lec 10 p. 11: {100} 51, {110} 57, {111} 1.25 µm/h, SiO₂ 0.004 µm/h. Only three orientations are given; all other planes use the linear three-rate interpolation (Radjenović et al. 2010, eq. 1) (assumption). Note: here {110} > {100}, while Lec 10 p. 16 orders EDP as (100) > (110) > (111).

etchants.name: EDP F&K 50:30:3, 110 °C
etchants.source: Ratio R(100):R(110):R(111) = 50:30:3 for EDP 'F&K' at 110 °C (Finne & Klein 1967, as listed in the Berkeley Microlab manual ch. 1.10); scaled so that R(100) = 51 µm/h as in Lec 10 p. 11 (assumption). Matches the order (100) > (110) > (111) of Lec 10 p. 16. Other planes: linear three-rate interpolation (assumption).

Q.source: EDP type S: Q(100) 0.40, Q(110) 0.33, Q(111) 0.52 eV (Seidel et al. 1990, Fig. 13, p. 3619); Q(SiO₂) 0.80 eV (Fig. 18, p. 3620). Used for the F&K composition too (assumption).
